stories.headline: Isaias aftermath: at least four dead, roofs torn off across the Panhandle, and the second-highest surge on record at Panama City Beach
stories.summary: Hurricane Isaias, the first hurricane of the Atlantic season, came ashore near Destin, Florida, about 9:30 p.m. ET Friday as a Category 2 storm with 105 mph winds, after briefly reaching Category 3 strength Friday morning. By Saturday it had weakened to a post-tropical cyclone moving inland toward Tennessee, but not before killing at least four people. In Florida, a woman died when a large tree fell onto her home, and a man was found dead in a garage in Escambia County after a generator was run indoors, with four others treated for carbon monoxide poisoning. In Alabama, a tree killed a person in a home in East Birmingham, and officials confirmed a second death in the state. Pensacola and nearby Milton were among the hardest hit, with apartment and store roofs peeled away and trees down on homes, and boats were tossed onto roads in Navarre and Tiger Point. Panama City Beach recorded its second-highest storm surge on record at 5.6 feet above average high tide. Heavy rain and confirmed tornadoes spread across Alabama, Georgia and South Carolina on Saturday.

stories.headline: ATF stops requiring federal approval and registration for suppressors and short-barreled rifles and shotguns — nationwide
stories.summary: Americans no longer need federal approval to make or own suppressors, short-barreled rifles, short-barreled shotguns and “any other weapons” under new ATF guidance issued Oct. 9. It ends a National Firearms Act approval system that has been in place for more than 90 years. The change follows the Silencer Shop Foundation v. ATF case. After the One Big Beautiful Bill Act cut the NFA tax on those items to zero on Jan. 1, U.S. District Judge Hendrix ruled that the approval and registration rules could no longer be justified under Congress’s taxing power, and the Justice Department chose not to appeal. The court order covered only the plaintiffs, but ATF Director Robert Cekada said the agency will apply it to everyone. ATF will also stop enforcing NFA registration and marking rules for these items and the ban on taking unregistered ones across state lines, though voluntary registration stays open. Machine guns and destructive devices are still fully regulated. Background checks, dealer rules and state bans, such as those in California, New Jersey and New York, still apply. Because the change rests on enforcement discretion rather than repeal, it could be reversed.

stories.headline: DOJ antitrust division probes ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox and NBC over their joint press-pool boycott after the White House ban
stories.summary: The Justice Department is investigating whether the five TV networks in the White House television pool (ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox and NBC) violated antitrust law when they jointly suspended pool coverage last month. They halted it in protest of President Trump pulling credentials from CNN, MS NOW and Politico. “Group boycotts among commercial competitors can violate the Sherman Act,” DOJ spokesperson Emily Covington told CBS News Saturday. “The Antitrust Division is simply investigating to determine whether these news organizations have violated the antitrust laws.” The suspension came during Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit. The networks said at the time that “no administration should reject a news organization because it objects to its reporting.” CNN, MS NOW and Politico won a temporary restraining order restoring their credentials, which Judge Timothy Kelly extended to Tuesday while he weighs the case, though CNN and Politico are still kept out of the Oval Office and off Air Force One. CBS noted it and CNN now share a parent company, Skydance, after the Paramount–Warner Bros. Discovery merger closed this week. The New York Times first reported the probe.

stories.headline: Houthi missile strike on Riyadh’s airport kills 12, including an American, and Trump says the U.S. ‘may’ join the Saudi fight
stories.summary: A missile struck King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday, killing at least 12 people and injuring 309, Saudi aviation authorities said. It was the deadliest attack on the kingdom in a decade and the worst on a Gulf Arab state since the Iran war began. The dead include one American, four Saudis and people from Bangladesh, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Sudan and the Palestinian territories; some of the wounded are critical, and the airport remained closed Sunday. Saudi Arabia, its allies and Washington blamed the Iran-backed Houthis, who did not immediately claim it but renewed a warning to stay away from Saudi airports; three people were killed in an earlier strike on the same airport Thursday. Asked whether the U.S. would join Saudi operations against the Houthis, President Trump said, “We may. We’re gonna look at it.” Egypt, Qatar, Germany and Canada condemned the strike, and U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres called it a violation of international law. Analysts warned the Houthis’ targeting has become markedly more effective, after a U.S. bombing campaign last year failed to stop them.

stories.headline: Erie, Pa., gunman kills seven relatives and a family friend, including a 22-month-old and a pregnant woman, then himself
stories.summary: A 45-year-old man killed seven members of his family and a family friend at a home in Erie, Pennsylvania, Friday evening before shooting himself, police said. Police Chief Rick Lorah called it “the worst scene I have ever experienced.” Officers responded just before 5 p.m. to a ShotSpotter alert and found two women, 51 and 37, dead outside. A neighbor’s Ring doorbell video showed them arriving distressed and pounding on doors for help, and its audio appears to capture muffled gunfire inside before the gunman came out and shot them. SWAT officers later breached the house with a robot and found a 5-year-old boy and a 22-month-old girl on the first floor, and four more victims, ages 19 to 44, in a stairwell. One victim was eight months pregnant. The shooter was found dead on the second floor with a .40-caliber handgun registered to him. Lorah said it is too soon to discuss motive but that he believes “mental health is at play here.” Gov. Josh Shapiro offered the state’s full support.

stories.headline: Pope Leo XIV says he will have surgery this week to remove a lung nodule found at a ‘very early stage’
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV told the crowd at his Sunday Angelus in St. Peter’s Square that doctors found a “localized nodule” in his lung at a “very early stage” and recommended removing it. “Following their advice, I have therefore decided to undergo an operation to remove it,” he said, asking for prayers. Vatican spokesperson Matteo Bruni said the operation is scheduled for the first days of this week at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital, the usual hospital for popes, with about a week of recovery expected. It is not yet clear whether the surgery will affect his trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru planned for early November. In the same address he appealed for safe passage of grain across the Black Sea (“The daily bread of millions of people cannot be held hostage by war”). On Saturday he posted that the death penalty is “inadmissible,” as the U.S. prepares to livestream the Fort Hood shooter’s execution.

stories.headline: Nearby Westport: Adrian Rodriguez’s hat trick sinks unbeaten Greenwich 3-0 as Staples boys soccer moves to 10-0-1
stories.summary: No fresh free Trumbull items turned up this weekend, so here is the nearby-town stand-in. Staples boys soccer, last year’s FCIAC and state champion, beat previously unbeaten Greenwich 3-0 at Cardinal Stadium behind a true hat trick (three straight goals) from Adrian Rodriguez, avenging a 4-3 comeback loss to the Cardinals in last year’s regular season. Greenwich came in 7-0-2. The win lifts the Wreckers to 10-0-1, with their fourth straight shutout and ninth of the season behind a tenacious defense and midfield. Staples has five league games left: Fairfield Ludlowe on Monday and Bridgeport Central on Wednesday, both at Wakeman Field at 4 p.m., then Brien McMahon on Saturday at 11:30 a.m.

stories.headline: Penguins snap their skid, beating Dallas 2-1 in a shootout behind Silovs as Kindel, Crosby and Rakell score
stories.summary: A night after a shootout loss at Columbus, the Penguins ground out a 2-1 shootout win over the Dallas Stars at home Saturday. It snapped an ugly skid and closed out a stretch of five games in eight days. Arturs Silovs started in goal, with Elmer Soderblom in for Ville Koivunen and Spencer Stastney replacing the injured Trevor van Riemsdyk. A Kris Letang goal in the first was wiped out on a Dallas challenge for a Hendrix Lapierre high stick. Connor Dewar broke the scoreless tie early in the third with his first of the season, a backhand off a Star in front that ended Jake Oettinger’s shutout streak of nearly 190 minutes. Tyler Seguin tied it with 29 seconds left on a deflection with Oettinger pulled. After a scoreless overtime, Ben Kindel and Sidney Crosby scored in the shootout, Wyatt Johnston kept Dallas alive, Rickard Rakell went top shelf in Round 4 and Silovs stopped Mikko Rantanen to win it. PensBurgh called it the team’s best all-around effort since the opening-night rout of the Flyers.

stories.headline: Hurricane Simon closes in on Mexico’s Pacific coast at 155 mph, just shy of Category 5, as Puerto Vallarta boards up
stories.summary: Hurricane Simon’s eye was just off Mexico’s Pacific coast early Sunday, about 60 miles west-southwest of Manzanillo and moving north-northwest at 6 mph, and was expected to come ashore later in the day. Its 155 mph winds are just below Category 5. Forecasters expect 10 to 20 inches of rain over parts of southwestern Mexico, and up to 30 inches in Michoacán, Colima and Jalisco, warning of “life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain,” along with a dangerous storm surge and destructive waves near and east of landfall. Jalisco suspended classes in 22 coastal municipalities, began evacuating people from at-risk areas and told the tourism sector in Puerto Vallarta, a popular destination for Americans, to make sure workers and visitors have shelter. Hotels and shops there were boarding up Saturday.

stories.headline: Tesla says its Austin Cybercab fleet grew 8x in a month to 300-plus, and names Dallas as the next city
stories.summary: Tesla has given its first official count of its active Cybercab fleet. The Robotaxi account posted Saturday that one month after launch the service had “scaled to 300+ Cybercabs serving Austin – an 8x increase in 30 days.” Tesla AI software chief Ashok Elluswamy added: “Two years since the 10/10 Cybercab WeRobot event, the cabs are everywhere in Austin now. Dallas soon,” the first time Tesla has named the next city for public Cybercab rides. Public rides opened in Austin on Sept. 4. The fleet passed 100 in late September after jumping from 58 to 125 vehicles in a single week, and on Thursday Tesla added 150 Cybercabs to the Texas automated-vehicle registry, raising its registered count from 169 to 319.

stories.headline: Bassist Becky Baldwin thought the email was fake: how she landed the gig on Tony Iommi’s solo album ‘From The Dark’
stories.summary: Mercyful Fate’s newest bassist, Becky Baldwin, 35, told The Chronicles Of Podcast how she ended up on Black Sabbath guitarist Tony Iommi’s upcoming solo album, “From The Dark.” The lineup also includes drummer Karl Brazil, known for work with Robbie Williams and James Blunt, and Norwegian singer Jørn Lande. She said an email arrived on “some random Wednesday” with “Tony Iommi” in the subject line, from someone saying they were Iommi’s manager and inviting her to the studio. “This is fake. Surely this is fake,” she recalled thinking, until she checked the sender, website and email and then called. It turned out producer Mike Exeter had been following her for years, including her classic-metal bass covers on social media, some of them Black Sabbath songs, and recommended her when Iommi went looking for a bassist.

stories.headline: Babylon Bee: ‘Heaven Excited To Finally Get Answer To Who Would Win A Fight Between God And Mike Ditka’
stories.summary: The Babylon Bee marks Mike Ditka’s death at 86 by settling the oldest Bears-fan debate. Heaven’s residents gather for the long-awaited “Ditka v. God” showdown. “We know Ditka would win against a hurricane,” one resident explains, and that it would be a tie against a hurricane named ‘Ditka.’ An increasingly exasperated angel tries to explain that the Lord is “the eternal source of all power and existence” and that every ounce of Ditka’s strength comes from Him. The fans reply that this only means a God-strengthened Ditka is unbeatable. The kicker: when Ditka kneels before the Lord in worship, Bears fans take it as a sign he is running out the clock on a victory.

stories.headline: Meet your Trumbull candidates: Town Council member Bill Mecca makes his case for the 123rd House District — fix the school-funding formula and get tough on utility costs
stories.summary: Bill Mecca, a Trumbull Town Council member running for state representative in the 123rd House District against incumbent David Rutigliano, answered Patch’s candidate questionnaire ahead of the Nov. 3 election. He calls K–12 school funding the No. 1 issue in Connecticut and wants the state to put in more money and rewrite the Education Cost Sharing formula so suburban towns like Trumbull don’t lean so heavily on property taxes, and to end unfunded state mandates. On electric bills, he backs a mix of nuclear, renewables and storage, using the Millstone and Seabrook contracts, and much tougher scrutiny of utility spending before it lands in rates. As evidence he can do the job, Mecca points to his time as president of the Nichols Improvement Association, where he started the Nichols Farmers Market and an adult kickball league, and his council votes for balanced budgets since 2018, restoring the police pension, keeping the town’s top-tier bond rating, a bigger tax break for volunteer firefighters and the senior-center referendum.

stories.headline: Tesoro’s October newsletter: free naloxone cabinets at five Trumbull spots, the Veterans and First Responders Center on track for January, and a $243,656 special-education grant
stories.summary: First Selectman Vicki Tesoro’s October newsletter, posted Friday, rounds up what is happening around town ahead of the Nov. 3 election. Trumbull’s prevention partnership, TPAUD, has worked with Catalyst CT to install five self-service cabinets that hand out free naloxone nasal spray around the clock, at the police department on Edison Road, the health department on White Plains Road, both library branches and Vaughn Family Dentistry on Corporate Drive. The Veterans and First Responders Center at Kaatz Pond off Whitney Avenue is due to be finished in January and will be available for public rental, and new sidewalks are going in on Whitney Avenue between Dunellen Road and the Pequonnock River Trail, with alternating one-lane traffic. The state’s signal work on White Plains Road between Daniels Farm Road and Reservoir Avenue is still causing delays. Public Works says 32 miles of roads were paved or sealed this season, with Williams Road paving still to come. The schools are getting $243,656 from a new state special-education grant. Early voting runs Oct. 19 to Nov. 1 at the Trumbull Library on Quality Street, and loose-leaf pickup is expected to start Nov. 4.

stories.headline: Krebs: the Canadian arrested in the FBI’s ShinyHunters probe is the co-founder of a ransomware-negotiation firm, seized while visiting a Philadelphia cyber-insurance summit
stories.summary: The Canadian man the FBI arrested in Pennsylvania this week in its investigation of the ShinyHunters hacking group, which stole data on thousands of FBI employees from the bureau’s job portal, appears to be a co-founder of a cybersecurity company that negotiates with ransomware gangs on behalf of victims, Brian Krebs reports. Sources told KrebsOnSecurity the suspect was in town for a cyber-insurance conference, and federal court records show an Edward Dobrovsky (a slight misspelling of Edward Dubrovsky, co-founder of Canadian firms Cypfer and CyberSteward) was arrested Oct. 8 on cyber-extortion and conspiracy charges; the case has been moved to the Eastern District of Texas, now the center of the probe. Dubrovsky wrote a book on handling ransomware negotiations. The FBI declined to comment. Krebs’s sources say charges against people at other negotiation firms may follow. The FBI says ShinyHunters has extorted more than $70 million this year; “Rey,” the member who took over the group after an earlier arrest, was reported detained in Jordan last week.

stories.headline: Buy an iPhone Duo at an Apple Store and it will greet you by name: ‘Hello, Steve’ on the first startup screen
stories.summary: Apple has a small surprise for people who buy the foldable iPhone Duo at a U.S. Apple Store: employees will be able to set the phone so it shows the buyer’s name on the “Hello” screen the first time it turns on, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports. The option is limited to the Duo in the U.S., with English and Spanish greetings. MacRumors expects it to cover both in-store purchases and orders picked up in a store. Preorders for the iPhone Duo open Oct. 16 at 8 a.m. Eastern, it goes on sale Oct. 23, and prices start at $1,999.

stories.headline: Brian May on Queen’s restored 1986 ‘Budapest’ concert film, Freddie’s last tour — and why a Queen reunion is ‘a big I don’t know’
stories.summary: Queen’s July 1986 show at Budapest’s 80,000-seat Népstadion, the first outdoor stadium concert by a Western rock band behind the Iron Curtain, has been restored in 4K for Queen Budapest, out on DVD and Blu-ray Oct. 30. Brian May and Roger Taylor tell Classic Rock the band arrived by hydrofoil down the Danube and that Freddie Mercury learned a Hungarian folk song for the crowd, reading the words off his hand; Taylor remembers Mercury asking whether the parliament building was for sale. It was the last tour: the band played its final show with Mercury at Knebworth less than three weeks later, and May recalls Freddie saying backstage, “I can’t do this any more after this.” Queen hasn’t played live since two shows in Japan in February 2024. May says another tour is “a big ‘I don’t know,’” but believes that if Mercury were alive, Queen would probably be touring next year.

stories.headline: ‘We thought it was the end’: severe turbulence sends a JFK-bound Avianca flight diving about 25,000 feet; it diverts to Miami and eight people are hospitalized
stories.summary: Avianca Flight 42 from Medellín, Colombia, to New York’s Kennedy Airport was diverted to Miami early Friday after hitting severe turbulence, and Miami-Dade Fire Rescue took eight people to the hospital. The airline said three crew members and six passengers were hurt. Passengers said the flight had been calm for about an hour and a half, with flight attendants handing out refreshments, when the plane suddenly dropped. “The flight attendant went flying,” said a passenger named Pilar, adding that people who weren’t wearing seat belts were thrown up too and ended up with cuts on their heads. “We thought it was the end for us.” FlightRadar24 data shows the Airbus A320 reached about 36,000 feet over Cuba before descending roughly 25,000 feet in minutes. The plane landed safely at 3:30 a.m., where six or seven ambulances were waiting. Avianca said it was rebooking the remaining passengers to New York. One passenger said she would rather just go home.

stories.headline: Leak: LEGO Pokémon blind boxes are coming March 1, 2027, at $12.99 each
stories.summary: LEGO’s new Pokémon line looks set to add blind boxes next spring, according to a leak from the account got.cooped reported by Game Rant. The boxes would go on sale March 1, 2027, at $12.99 each. LEGO hasn’t announced them, and it isn’t clear what will be inside. Fans are guessing either small brick-built Pokémon, possibly compatible with LEGO’s Smart Brick, or minifigures of gym leaders and trainers, which only a handful of characters have gotten so far. The Pokémon Company moved from Mega Bloks to LEGO at the start of 2026 and several sets have come out since. With more than 1,000 Pokémon and the next generation of games, Pokémon Winds and Waves, due in 2027, blind boxes would be a cheap way to cover characters that might not justify a bigger set.

stories.headline: 2027 Jeep Grand Cherokee build-and-price is live: Laredo from $41,515, a bigger standard screen, new colors, and Trailhawk and Overland coming
stories.summary: Jeep has quietly opened its online Build & Price configurator for the 2027 Grand Cherokee and three-row Grand Cherokee L, and orders are open with dealer arrivals expected in late 2026. Laredo and Laredo X keep the 3.6-liter Pentastar V6, while Laredo Altitude and up use the turbocharged 2.0-liter Hurricane4 four-cylinder. Base trims get a welcome upgrade to a standard 10.1-inch Uconnect 5 screen (up from 8.4 inches) and redesigned 18-inch wheels; Limited adds 20-inch wheels, wireless charging and rain-sensing wipers. Towing tops out at 6,200 pounds. Trailhawk and Overland return later, and a new cheaper off-road Laredo Upland is coming. High Gloss Black and Sting Gray are new colors, with Ghost, Red Hot, Olive Green and others due later. Pricing, including $1,995 destination: Laredo two-row from $41,515, Trailhawk from $54,995 and Overland from $57,895.
